speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are a newborn presenting with respiratory distress; tell me, how many days old are you, and has your mother had any recent infections or complications during pregnancy?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history. Given that you were born at 33 weeks with respiratory distress just two hours after delivery, are you experiencing nasal flaring, grunting, or retractions? I will also need to review your physical examination findings.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Grunting, Intercoastal and subcostal retractions, Peripheral cyanosis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The presence of grunting and significant retractions with peripheral cyanosis in a 33-weeker is highly suggestive of Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS). To confirm this, I must see the lung pattern on imaging.

REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS)
